The CFRU ability pop-up upper-line routine copies the battler's nickname from party data (bl 0x89C00A0, + 8) into a 13-byte stack buffer at sp + 0x28.
The buffer is cleared at 0x9A8F16, and copy loop 0x9A8F20-0x9A8F32 runs up to the terminator.
At the terminator it stores movs r2, #0xB4 (’, record 0 at 0x9A8F44) with strb r2, [r3].
Unless the last letter is 0xCD or 0xE7 (S, s: cmp at 0x9A8F4A, 0x9A8F4E), it stores movs r2, #0xE7 (s, record 1 at 0x9A8F52) with strb r2, [r3, #1].
It then stores 0xFF at 0x9A8F58-0x9A8F5E, and bl 0x89A57C4 at 0x9A8F8E prints the buffer.
Each record is the immediate byte, and the opcode byte 0x22 after it stays.
With 0xFF in record 0, the first store ends the name, and subsequent stores stay within the same 13 bytes behind the terminator.
The search for movs #0xB4 followed within 22 bytes by movs #0xE7 finds no other code.

The Unbound berry blender (see berry_blender_possessive) uses StringAppend to append sp + 0x18 for a nickname that ends in S or s, or is empty.
The buffer is built by movs r3, #0xB4 (’, the record's immediate byte), add r2, sp, #0x18 and strh r3, [r2] (’ and 0x00, a space).
The opcode byte 0x23 after the immediate stays.
Then adds r3, #0x4B and strb r3, [r2, #2] at 0x1EBB938-0x1EBB940 make the terminator the immediate + 0x4B.
Only 0xB4 (’, the English '’ ') and 0xFF (empty) keep the text terminated.
With 0xFF, the first byte ends the text, and the bytes behind it stay in the same 3-byte buffer.
This record serves Latin names ending in S or s.
